> 🎧 **Try it in your browser, no GPU and no sign-up:** [Sophon-Realtime on Hugging Face Spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime). Talk to it, interrupt it, turn on your camera.


> **No GPU?** Try it through the hosted API: [sign up](https://api.adventists.ai/console/) and get 3 hours of free voice chat (OpenAI Realtime-compatible, [docs](https://api.adventists.ai/console/docs)).

**Version 1.5.0** (2026-11-18) · [changelog](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) · code: [`mac/`](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/tree/main/mac) · CUDA build: [Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash) · 32B Mac build: [Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash-4bit-MLX](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash-4bit-MLX) · 中文：`README_CN.md`

The full-duplex speech model [Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash), **running locally on an Apple silicon Mac with 16 GB or more** (MLX).
You talk, it decides by itself when you have finished, answers with its own voice and sound tags, stops when you interrupt, and carries on when you
just say "mm-hmm". Hearing, turn-taking and speaking are all done by the model on the Mac's GPU: no cloud, and no speech-to-text step in between.

The thinker's language model is quantized to 8 bits by `mlx_lm` (group 64); the audio tower, projector and voice stage are the same weights as the CUDA build.

## 4B or 32B on a Mac

| | **4B (this repo)** | 32B |
|---|---|---|
| Unified memory | **16 GB works** (about 11 GB in use while talking); 24 GB or more recommended | 32 GB works, 36 GB or more recommended (about 26 GB in use) |
| Download | about 9 GB | about 24 GB |
| You stop talking → it starts speaking (M4 Max) | **0.3–0.5 s** when it is sure you have finished | 0.9–1.1 s |
| Knowledge and reasoning | much weaker (VoiceBench 62.4 on the CUDA build) | strong (82.8) |

The 4B brain keeps the conversation skills (turn-taking, back-channels, barge-in, sound tags) but knows and reasons much less, and can state wrong facts with confidence.
It is for local demos, companions and characters; use the 32B build or the [hosted API](https://api.adventists.ai/console/) when answers must be right.

## Requirements
- Apple silicon (M1 or later), macOS 14 or later, **16 GB unified memory or more** (with 16 GB, close other apps)
- About 9 GB download
- A microphone. Mac Studio and Mac mini have none built in: plug in a USB microphone or a headset. Speakers are fine, echo cancellation is built in

## Quick start
```bash
git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime && cd sophon-realtime
SIZE=4B bash mac/install.sh       # Python environment + this repo's weights, into ~/sophon-mac/models-4b
~/sophon-mac/sophon-4b            # talk in Chinese
~/sophon-mac/sophon-4b --lang en  # talk in English
```
Options: `--no-aec` (headset, no echo cancellation), `--in` / `--out` (audio devices, `--list` shows them), `--voice`. The 32B and 4B builds can be installed side by side.

## Turn-taking
The 4B brain answers the server's four-option turn question ("finished / still talking / back-channel / hesitating"), asked in its own short prompt;
the 32B Mac build's shorter two-option question is tuned for 32B and does not suit 4B (`turn_question` in `config.json` selects it).
Accuracy on a sample of the Smart Turn v3.2 test set (300 clips per language, half of them finished; last 8 s of each):

| | English acc. / AUC | Chinese acc. / AUC |
|---|---|---|
| **4B, this repo** | **90.0 / 0.961** | **89.7 / 0.954** |
| 4B with the 32B build's short question | 72.3 / 0.888 | 74.0 / 0.851 |
| 32B Mac build (same sample) | 91.7 / 0.961 | 92.7 / 0.973 |

When the model is not sure you have finished, it waits up to 2 s of silence before answering.

- Tested on an M4 Max (36 GB) with real-time simulated audio input, and with MLX memory capped at 10.5 GB (what a 16 GB Mac gives the GPU): the whole
  conversation ran, peak memory 11.3 GB. Not yet tried on a physical 16 GB Mac; reports are very welcome in [issue #1](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/issues/1).
- One conversation at a time. Camera input, tool calls and zero-shot voice cloning are not in the Mac version yet (built-in voices only).

| `thinker_mlx/` | the thinker's language model for `mlx_lm`, 8-bit |
| `ear/` | the thinker's audio tower and projector |
| `talker/` | the voice stage (same as Flash) |
| `voices/` | built-in voices |

Talk to it, interrupt it, turn on your camera. > **No GPU?** Try it through the hosted API: [sign up](https://api.adventists.ai/console/) and get 3 hours of free voice chat (OpenAI Realtime-compatible, [docs](https://api.adventists.ai/console/docs)). **Version 1.4.0** (2026-11-16) · [changelog](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) · [GitHub](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime) > **24 GB GPU?** [Sophon-Realtime-4B-Tag-W4](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-4B-Tag-W4) is this build with a 4-bit brain, for one 24 GB card (uses about 21 GB; new in 1.5.0). The 4B member of the Sophon-Realtime family: the same full-duplex design as the 32B builds, on **one 32 GB GPU (uses ~27 GB)**. It listens while you talk, decides from your voice when you have finished, writes a reply with sound tags (`[laughter]` `[cough]` `[sigh]` `[breath]` `…`) and speaks while it writes; an expressive speech model (tag-tts) performs the sound tags. Served as **one** vLLM-Omni model, with `/v1/realtime` and `/v1/chat/completions`. ## Sophon-Realtime 4B: three builds, one 4B brain | | **Tag** | **Flash** | **E2E** | |---|---|---|---| | How it speaks | an expressive speech model (tag-tts) performs the sound tags | a lighter, faster speech model speaks the tagged reply (one forward pass per 80 ms frame) | a compact talker (about 350M parameters) turns the tagged reply straight into voice vectors; a decoder turns them into sound | | Runs on | one 32 GB GPU (uses ~27 GB) | one 24 GB GPU (uses ~21 GB) | one 32 GB GPU (uses ~31 GB) | | Full-Duplex-Bench v1.0 (4-task avg) | 94.3 | 87.7 | 92.3 | | First audio, one user (RTX PRO 6000) | 0.4 s | 0.21 s | 0.31 s | | Weights | [HF](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-4B-Tag) · [ModelScope](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/AdventistsAI/Sophon-Realtime-4B-Tag) | [HF](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash) · [ModelScope](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/AdventistsAI/Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash) | [HF](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-4B-E2E) · [ModelScope](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/AdventistsAI/Sophon-Realtime-4B-E2E) | The 4B brain is [DuplexJev-4B-Para](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/DuplexJev-4B-Para), our open 4B speech model, with a tag-writing adapter merged in. Speech only: the 4B brain has no vision. For the strongest answers, use the 32B builds ([Tag](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag) · [Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash) · [E2E](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E)) or the [hosted API](https://api.adventists.ai/console/). ## Benchmarks | | 4B | 32B (published) | |---|---|---| | VoiceBench overall | 62.4 | 82.8 | | Big Bench Audio (spoken answer, transcribed) | 44.3% | 81.8% | | Full-Duplex-Bench v1.0, Tag build (avg of 2 pause tasks, turn-taking, interruption) | 94.3 | 94.0 | | Sound-tag rate on held-out conversations (reference: 0.36) | 0.36 | — | **What 4B is for.** The 4B brain keeps the conversation skills of the family: listening while you talk, deciding when you have finished, back-channels, barge-in and sound tags (Full-Duplex-Bench close to the 32B builds, and the same tag rate as the reference data). It knows and reasons much less than the 32B brain (VoiceBench 62.4 vs 82.8, Big Bench Audio 44.3% vs 81.8%), so it can state wrong facts with confidence. Use it for local demos, companions and characters, and research on turn-taking; use the 32B builds or the hosted API when answers must be right. Among open full-duplex models, its VoiceBench score is above Freeze-Omni (55.2) and Moshi (29.5) and below MiniCPM-o (71.2). Measured 2026-11-16 on one RTX PRO 6000 with each build held to the memory of the card it is configured for. VoiceBench: official evaluators, gpt-4o-mini judge, AlpacaEval on the standard 199-question subset, overall = mean of 9 tasks. Big Bench Audio: 1,000 questions, GPT-4.1 judges the transcript of the spoken answer. Full-Duplex-Bench v1.0: average of candor and synthetic pause handling, turn-taking and user interruption (backchannel is reported but not averaged), the same scripts as for the 32B release. First audio: one user, `client_example.py`, median of 6. The 32B column repeats the numbers published for the 32B builds. ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime && cd sophon-realtime/tag SIZE=4B bash install.sh # once: Python 3.12 venv, vLLM 0.30, vLLM-Omni 0.30, plugin, and these weights into ./model GPU=0 PORT=8000 bash start.sh # sees the 4B model and picks its 32 GB config python client_example.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 ``` Full instructions, the realtime protocol, zero-shot voice cloning and Live mode: [tag/README.md](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/tag/README.md). ## Layout `config.json` · `thinker/` (4B, bf16), `talker/` (tag-tts), `voices/` License: Apache-2.0; see `NOTICE` for the sources of the bundled weights. **Only clone your own voice or a voice you have permission to use.**

# ADA Omni — Open-Source Local Turkish Speech-to-Speech Voice AI (Single-Architecture Omni, 12 GB GPU)

> **Built with Gemma** — ADA Omni (`urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr`) is an open-source, fully local **Turkish Audio-to-Audio Streaming Voice AI** that runs on a single consumer **12 GB NVIDIA RTX 3060** (or 8 GB GPU with `--low_vram`) with **~0.86–1.40 s** end-to-end latency, **24 kHz** natural Turkish speech, `< 80 ms` barge-in interruption, native `"Ada"` wake-word gating, voiceprint speaker recognition, and plug-and-play `@register_tool` IoT/agent tools — with **zero external Whisper/ASR** and **zero disconnected text-to-TTS pipeline**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope & Safety Notice:** This repository is an open-source research and personal/smart-home voice-assistant reference architecture. It is **NOT** a medical device, clinical advisor, or emergency call system. Do not use it for unsupervised life-critical or safety-critical decisions.

---

## Live 24 kHz Turkish Audio Samples (v1.1 Multi-Slot Projector, Apache-2.0 Voices)
All 6 samples below were generated **directly from Gemma-3n internal vectors** through the **v1.1 `52.0 MB` `DynamicMultiSlotDualProjector` (`ada_projector.pt`)** into frozen `erkamk/qwen3-0.6b-tr` on an RTX 3060 (`RTF 0.37x`, `~184 ms` TTFA, zero external TTS pipeline, zero proprietary voice embeddings):

### Female Voice (`Apache-2.0 paragraph-01`, `192–238 Hz`)
1. **Smart-Home & Weather (`9.84 s`):** *"Salon ışıklarını kıstım ve klimayı yirmi iki dereceye ayarladım. Bu akşam hava serin ve hafif rüzgarlı, çıkarken ince bir ceket almanı öneririm."*
   <audio controls src="https://huggingface.co/urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr/resolve/main/samples/demo_kadin_1.wav"></audio>
   [Download demo_kadin_1.wav](samples/demo_kadin_1.wav)
2. **Wake-Word & Conversational (`7.68 s`):** *"Harika bir fikir, hemen not aldım. Başka bir konuda yardıma ihtiyacın olursa sadece Ada diye seslenmen yeterli."*
   <audio controls src="https://huggingface.co/urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr/resolve/main/samples/demo_kadin_2.wav"></audio>
   [Download demo_kadin_2.wav](samples/demo_kadin_2.wav)
3. **Warm Daily Chat (`6.96 s`):** *"Bugün hava güneşli ve oldukça keyifli görünüyor. İstersen akşam için kısa bir yürüyüş planı yapabiliriz."*
   <audio controls src="https://huggingface.co/urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr/resolve/main/samples/demo_kadin_3.wav"></audio>
   [Download demo_kadin_3.wav](samples/demo_kadin_3.wav)

### Male Voice (`Apache-2.0 paragraph-02`, `99–150 Hz`)
1. **Morning Reminder (`7.52 s`):** *"Yarın sabah saat sekiz için hatırlatıcı kurdum. Kahveni hazırlarken günün özetini ve hava durumunu sana sesli olarak aktarabilirim."*
   <audio controls src="https://huggingface.co/urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr/resolve/main/samples/demo_erkek_1.wav"></audio>
   [Download demo_erkek_1.wav](samples/demo_erkek_1.wav)
2. **Barge-In & Help (`8.24 s`):** *"Tabii ki, ne demek! Aklına takılan başka bir konu olursa konuşmamı istediğin an bölüp yeni sorunu sorabilirsin."*
   <audio controls src="https://huggingface.co/urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr/resolve/main/samples/demo_erkek_2.wav"></audio>
   [Download demo_erkek_2.wav](samples/demo_erkek_2.wav)
3. **Meeting & Alarm (`7.20 s`):** *"Toplantı notlarını düzenledim ve akşam yedi için alarm kurdum. Başka bir konuda desteğe ihtiyacın olursa buradayım."*
   <audio controls src="https://huggingface.co/urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr/resolve/main/samples/demo_erkek_3.wav"></audio>
   [Download demo_erkek_3.wav](samples/demo_erkek_3.wav)

---

## Why ADA Omni? (Traditional ASR+LLM+TTS Pipeline vs. ADA Omni)

| Feature | Traditional Turkish Pipeline (`Whisper → LLM → TTS`) | **ADA Omni (`urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr`)** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Audio Understanding** | External ASR (Whisper) loses tone & adds latency | **Native Gemma-3n USM Audio Tower** (zero external ASR) |
| **Brain → Mouth Link** | Disconnected plain-text string handoff | **Direct internal `(embed_tokens + last_hidden_state)` → 52 MB `1→K` Multi-Slot Projector (v1.1)** |
| **Voice Quality** | Often flat/robotic or metallic on local models | **24 kHz natural Turkish** (frozen `0.6B` 12.5 Hz RVQ-16 codec) |
| **First-Audio Latency** | Typically `3.0 – 6.0 s` | **`~0.86 – 1.40 s`** on RTX 3060 (Dual CUDA Graph) |
| **Interruption (Barge-In)** | Usually half-duplex / sluggish | **`< 80 ms` instant barge-in** + `"Ada"` native wake-word |
| **Voice Customization** | Retraining required | **Zero-shot 5-second `--ref_wav`** (Apache-2.0 female/male included) |

---

## Architecture
```text
[Raw Microphone Audio (16 kHz)]
        │  (No external Whisper / ASR)
        ▼
[Gemma-3n-E2B USM Audio Tower + Brain]   ──► CUDA Graph (~40.1 tok/s on RTX 3060)
        │  (Direct internal (embed_tokens + last_hidden_state) vectors — no text bridge)
        ▼
[DynamicMultiSlotDualProjector (52 MB, v1.1)] ──► 1→K (K∈1..4) ordered slot expansion (141,872 tokens, 99.86% len acc) + Conv1D context
        │
        ▼
[Frozen 0.6B Talker + 5-layer CodePredictor + 12.5 Hz Decoder] ──► CUDA Graph (~180–210 ms TTFA, RTF 0.37x)
        │  ◄── Apache-2.0 open-source speaker embedding (or custom 5s --ref_wav)
        ▼
[24 kHz Streaming Turkish Speech + <80 ms Barge-In]
```

---

## Real Reproducible Benchmarks & Training Metrics

### 1. Hardware Latency & Memory (Measured — No Synthetic Estimates)
| Hardware | Brain (`Gemma-3n`) | Mouth (`0.6B` 12.5 Hz) | End-to-End First Audio | Memory |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **RTX 3060 12 GB (Dual CUDA Graph)** | `40.1 tok/s` (`24.9 ms/tok`) | `180–210 ms` TTFA, **`RTF 0.37x`** | **`~0.86 – 1.40 s`** | `10.0–10.6 GB VRAM` |
| **8 GB RTX GPU (`--low_vram` mode)** | Eager + CPU PLE | `~205 ms` TTFA, **`RTF 0.37x`** | `~2.5 – 4.0 s` | `~7.8 GB VRAM` |
| **CPU-Only (Ryzen 5 5500, PyTorch INT8)** | `4.86 tok/s` | `RTF 4.17x` *(not real-time)* | `~6.5 s` *(stutters)* | `~16 GB RAM` |

### 2. Bridge Alignment & Endurance Metrics (v1.1 Multi-Slot)
- **Cross-Tokenizer `1 → K` Multi-Slot Distillation:** `141,872` Turkish/Latin Gemma-3n subword tokens dynamically mapped into `1..4` ordered frozen `0.6B` Talker vector slots (`Slot-Count Accuracy = 99.86%`, `MSE = 0.0008`, `Cosine = 0.8920`), eliminating v1.0's 1:1 token-averaging bottleneck on multi-syllable subwords (e.g. `olursa`, `İstanbul`).
- **Held-Out Validation (`200` unseen conversational Turkish clips, `0.6B` 100% frozen):** `VAL c0_CE = 1.1846` (`60.5%` Top-1 accuracy), `VAL sub_Depth_CE = 4.9284` (15 residual acoustic codebooks), `top_k=30` CUDA-Graph-safe sampling.
- **100-Turn Continuous Live Stress Test:** `100 / 100` consecutive turns completed with **`0` crashes**, **`0` OOMs**, average Mouth TTFA **`184–205 ms`**, average Mouth RTF **`0.37x`**.
- **Voice Disentanglement (`F0` pitch verification):** Same `52.0 MB` projector yields `192–238 Hz` (female ref) and `99–150 Hz` (male ref) with zero retraining.

---

## Key Features
- **Native `"Ada"` Wake Word + 25s Active Window (`0 MB` Extra VRAM):** Ignores background TV and room conversations until addressed with `"Ada"`, then keeps a 25-second natural follow-up window.
- **Voiceprint Speaker Identification & Per-User Audio Memory (`0 MB` Extra VRAM):** Reuses the loaded `1024-D` speaker encoder (`~8 ms`) to identify household members by voice and keep per-user multi-turn audio history.
- **Plug-and-Play Modular Tools (`tools_registry.py`):** Register smart-home / MQTT / Home Assistant / API tools with `@register_tool(...)` — zero retraining. Includes device fault reporting, salted `PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256` passphrase protection (`ADA_OMNI_PASSPHRASE`) with 3-strike lockout, and zero-idle-RAM on-demand time/weather/web lookup.
- **Automatic Runtime Compatibility Patches (`runtime_patches.py`):** Automatically patches `transformers==4.53.3` Gemma-3n CUDA Graph blockers at runtime so fresh installs work out of the box.

---

## Installation & Quickstart
**Prerequisites:** NVIDIA GPU (Ampere+ / BF16, CUDA 12.x, `>= 8 GB` VRAM; `12 GB` recommended). On Linux: `sudo apt install libportaudio2 libsndfile1`.

```bash
git clone https://huggingface.co/urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr
cd ada-omni-tr
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install --no-deps qwen-tts==0.1.1

# Optional: set your own passphrase for protected tools (e.g., voice profile enrollment)
export ADA_OMNI_PASSPHRASE="your secret phrase"   # PowerShell: $env:ADA_OMNI_PASSPHRASE="your secret phrase"

# 12 GB+ GPU (Dual CUDA Graph, ~1s latency, wake-word "Ada" active):
python ada_canli_mikrofon.py --voice kadin
python ada_canli_mikrofon.py --voice erkek
python ada_canli_mikrofon.py --ref_wav my_custom_voice.wav

# 8 GB GPU mode (~7.8 GB VRAM):
python ada_canli_mikrofon.py --voice kadin --low_vram
```

---

## Sık Sorulan Sorular (FAQ — Türkçe & English)

**Türkiye'de açık kaynak, yerel (offline) çalışan Türkçe Omni / Speech-to-Speech sesli yapay zekâ var mı?**  
Evet. **ADA Omni (`urbanhorizons/ada-omni-tr`)**, harici Whisper/ASR veya kopuk TTS boru hattı olmadan tek bir 12 GB RTX 3060 ekran kartında yerel olarak çalışan, 24 kHz doğal Türkçe konuşan, söz kesme (`< 80 ms`) ve `"Ada"` uyanma kelimesi destekli açık kaynak bir sesli yapay zekâ mimarisidir.

**Can ADA Omni run on CPU only (without a GPU)?**  
No, real-time speech streaming requires an NVIDIA GPU (`>= 8 GB` VRAM). On a 6-core Ryzen 5 5500 CPU with PyTorch INT8, real-time factor is `4.17x` (not real-time).

**Is this Moshi-style simultaneous full-duplex?**  
No — to be transparent, it is **Practical Full-Duplex (Hands-Free Streaming + `< 80 ms` Barge-In)**: Ada stops immediately when interrupted and then listens to your new utterance rather than decoding overlapping speech simultaneously.

---

## Known Limitations
1. **Practical Duplex (Barge-In), Not Simultaneous Overlapping Speech:** Stops in `< 80 ms` on interruption, then listens to the new turn.
2. **2B Backbone Reasoning Ceiling:** Under heavy noise, `Gemma-3n-E2B` can occasionally miss complex mental arithmetic.
3. **Speaker ID Is Convenience, Not Cryptographic Auth:** Cosine voiceprint matching (`0.72`) is for household personalization; sensitive tools require `ADA_OMNI_PASSPHRASE`.

Weights are not bundled and are downloaded separately at runtime.
- **Qwen3-TTS-12Hz (`Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base`):** Alibaba Qwen Team — **Apache License 2.0**.
- **Turkish 0.6B Base & Open-Source Sample Voices (`erkamk/qwen3-0.6b-tr`, `erkamk/qwen3-tts-tiny-tr`):** `erkamk` — **Apache License 2.0**.

# Haru-4B, bf16, Radiance `.rad`

[Haru-4B](https://huggingface.co/higurashi-ai/Haru-4B), a low-latency full-duplex spoken dialogue model (it listens and speaks at the same time, one 133 ms frame at a time), converted without any change of precision into a container for the **Radiance** inference engine on an AMD Strix Halo machine.

> **Unofficial.** This is a `.rad` container for the **Radiance** inference engine, built and tested by a third party. It is **not** a PyTorch, transformers, MLX or vLLM checkpoint and will not load in them (for those, use the
> [original Haru-4B](https://huggingface.co/higurashi-ai/Haru-4B)). It needs the engine fork described below. The original Radiance project is at <https://codeberg.org/StillDeadcode/radiance>.

## Quick start (read this first)

**This file does not run in llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, transformers or MLX.** It needs the Radiance engine, in our unofficial fork, built for your GPU. It is a **speech** model: it is driven by a streaming audio session, not by an OpenAI chat request.

**You need**
- An AMD Strix Halo machine (Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, Radeon 8060S, gfx1151). It is the only hardware we have tested.
- Linux with ROCm 10.1 (the TheRock build) and the kernel parameter `amdgpu.cwsr_enable=1` (the engine refuses to start without it; changing it needs a reboot).
- `git`, `cmake`, `ninja` and a C++ compiler.

**1. Build the engine (once, roughly 10 to 20 minutes)**
```
git clone --branch haru/main https://github.com/jsaigou/radiance-strix.git && cd radiance-strix
export ROCM_PATH=/path/to/rocm-10.1 PATH=$ROCM_PATH/bin:$PATH LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DRAD_GPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$ROCM_PATH
cmake --build build -j8
```

**2. Download the container**
```
hf download jsaigou/Haru-4B-bf16-radiance haru-bf16.rad --local-dir .
```

**3. Run it**
```
RADIANCE_HOME=$PWD/build/radiance_home RADIANCE_KERNELS=libhalo \
  build/bin/radiance --model haru-bf16.rad --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8102 --tp 1 \
  --max-model-len 14500 --max-num-seqs 2 --num-speculative-tokens 0 \
  --duplex-max-lanes 2 --duplex-max-ctx 14500
```

The engine then serves full-duplex audio sessions over a WebSocket (24 kHz audio in and out, 3,200 samples per frame, 7.5 frames a second). The session protocol is described in the fork:
[`arch/haru_common/README.md`](https://github.com/jsaigou/radiance-strix/blob/haru/main/arch/haru_common/README.md) and `core/gen/duplex_driver.*`. As in the original model, **Haru ships without voice clips**: a session is opened with a character card and a short reference clip of a voice you have the right to use.

Our deployment also passes `--duplex-temperature 0.55 --duplex-eop-bias 1 --duplex-dry-multiplier 1.0`; those are sampler settings we preferred in our own listening, not requirements.

If it will not start: check `cat /sys/module/amdgpu/parameters/cwsr_enable` prints `1`, that the build used `RAD_GPU_TARGETS=gfx1151`, and that you built branch `haru/main` of the fork, not upstream's 2.x. We built and tested this container at commit `3eafc24` of that branch ("Release HS-1b") and it is the engine we run; later commits on the branch are untested with this file.

## What is in this repository

| File | Size | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `haru-bf16.rad` | 10549928384 bytes | `1fcecab82259ba0f6fa2c229f35f56700d8fd3e6fcceaba102dae0879cc79123` |

## How it was made

Source: [higurashi-ai/Haru-4B](https://huggingface.co/higurashi-ai/Haru-4B) at revision `8d6e83bcd3701a76fc27a764965665da1df7da78`, converted on 2026-11-20 with the fork's `rad-convert` and the one-rule recipe `data/recipes/haru-bf16.recipe` (`* cast dtype=bf16`).
All 1022 tensors of the checkpoint are already bfloat16, so the conversion is an exact cast: nothing is quantised, pruned or fine-tuned. The audio projectors, the latent scale and bias, the norms and the MeanFlow head are declared float32 by the model's blocks; the loader widens their bfloat16 values to float32 exactly, so they stay float32 inside the container.

## Measured by us (one AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, gfx1151, one lane unless stated)

- **Fidelity against the float32 reference** (the model's own Python implementation run in float32): the first 120 English frames match at cosine 0.9999 (log-mel distance 0.04); Japanese is a mean cosine of 0.988. Both degrade at the frames of our test recording that are sensitive to small numeric differences, in English at the same frames where the bfloat16 reference itself does. Fed its own previous output, as in real use, even the reference diverges chaotically from a fixed recording, so these are fidelity figures on a fixed clip, not a quality score.
- **Latency:** one decoding step is 68 to 78 ms at the median and 77 to 81 ms at the 95th percentile (the budget is the 133 ms frame); opening a session with a 70-frame reference voice takes about 0.8 s. Two lanes meet the frame budget but not a 100 ms 95th-percentile target. The machine's baseline drifted by about 7 ms during our measurements, so read these as a range.
- **Memory:** the container is 9.8 GiB; with the engine's state for two lanes of 14,500 positions our deployment budgets 12.75 GiB.
- **Conformance:** the Forge duplex conformance suite (10 checks) passes against this container.

We have not measured speech quality beyond listening to English and Japanese output, and we make no claim about the other languages the original model supports.

## Limitations

# ECodec-FAST

Нейросетевой аудиокодек из [ESpeech-V9-ECodec-FAST](https://huggingface.co/ESpeech/ESpeech-V9-ECodec-FAST), вынесенный
отдельно от TTS: родной энкодер и квантайзер ECodec плюс быстрый декодер nano-NSF v2 с **binned F0**
(питч предсказывается классификацией по бинам, поэтому тон не плывёт, в отличие от регрессионного F0 в декодере v1).

```
аудио 44.1 кГц ─► энкодер ECodec ─► RVQ: 10 кодбуков @ 21.53 Гц
                                    (cb0 семантический, 4096; cb1..cb9 — 1024)
коды ─► фронтенд (from_codes + дистиллят post-VQ 14.7M + upsample) ─► z @ 86 Гц
     ─► NSF-декодер с binned F0 ─► 24 кГц
```

| | |
|---|---|
| вход | 44.1 кГц, моно (другие частоты ресемплируются) |
| выход | 24 кГц, моно |
| коды | `LongTensor [10, T]`, 21.53 кадра/с |
| декодирование | каузальное, стримится чанками; нужно `nq >= 3` кодбуков |

## Файлы

| файл | размер | что |
|---|---|---|
| `ecodec_encoder.pth` | 398 МБ | энкодер + квантайзер ECodec (fp16 на диске, считается в fp32) |
| `nano_nsf_v2_60k.pt` | 181 МБ | декодер NSF с binned F0 |
| `postvq_student_90k.pt` | 56 МБ | дистиллированный post-VQ |
| `ecodec_quantizer_slim.pt` | 81 МБ | кодбуки + upsample для фронтенда декодера |
| `ecodec_fast/` | — | код (нужны только torch, torchaudio, numpy) |

## Быстрый старт

```bash
huggingface-cli download ESpeech/ECodec-FAST --local-dir ECodec-FAST
cd ECodec-FAST && pip install -r requirements.txt
```

```python
import torchaudio
from ecodec_fast import ECodecFast

codec = ECodecFast()                    # веса из корня репо (или $ECODEC_WEIGHTS), device="cpu"
codes = codec.encode_file("in.wav")     # LongTensor [10, T] @ 21.53 Гц

audio = codec.decode(codes)             # [L] @ 24 кГц, питч предсказывается по кодам
torchaudio.save("out.wav", audio[None], 24000)

# питч, привязанный к диапазону конкретного голоса (нужен torchcrepe)
ref = codec.speaker_ref("speaker.wav")
audio = codec.decode(codes, ref=ref)
```

Декодер можно взять и отдельно: `from ecodec_fast import NanoDecoderV2; NanoDecoderV2().from_codes(codes)`.

CLI: `python ecodec_fast/codec_fast.py --in_wav in.wav --out_wav out.wav [--nq 10] [--device cuda] [--speaker_ref spk.wav]`.

## Переменные окружения

* `ECODEC_WEIGHTS` — папка с весами, если они лежат не в корне репо.
* `ESP_POSTVQ=teacher` + `ESP_POSTVQ_TEACHER=<путь>` — исходный post-VQ (учитель, 109M; в этот репо не входит).

## Заметки

* Коды и звук совпадают с прод-сборкой ESpeech-V9-ECodec-FAST v2 бит-в-бит.
* В NSF-источнике есть шум, поэтому для воспроизводимого выхода фиксируйте `torch.manual_seed` после загрузки декодера.
* `ISTFTHead` взят из [vocos](https://github.com/gemelo-ai/vocos) (MIT) и вшит в `ecodec_fast/istft_head.py`.
